A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the eider duck cerebrocortical neurons have a very high tolerance towards hypoxia/anoxic stress, but that the cerebellar neurons have a slightly lower tolerance, which is due to a different response to hypoxaemia.

KATP-channel-mediated responses to hypoxia may not be universal in vertebrates, and that other mechanisms must exist to explain the hypoxic/ischaemic tolerance in eider ducks.
